Cc.name: Copernican Crater
Cc.desc: Rim, wall and floor deposits of craters with sharp prominent rims, circular to polygonal outlines. High relative brightness and rays.

Ccc.name: Crater, Catena
Ccc.desc: Elongated linear clusters of overlapping circular to semi-circular.

Csc.name: Copernican Crater, Secondary
Csc.desc: Small to very small diameter craters, densely spaced near and/or on the ejecta blanket of craters.

Ec.name: Eratosthenian Crater
Ec.desc: Non-rayed, circular craters with sharp to partially subdued crater rim crests, partial circumferential ejecta present, and lower albedo compared to unit Cc.

Ecc.name: Eratosthenian Crater, Catena
Ecc.desc: Elongated linear to elliptical clusters of circular to semi-circular depressions, often overlapping.

Esc.name: Eratosthenian Secondary Crater
Esc.desc: Small to very small diameter craters, densely spaced near and/or on the ejecta blanket of craters.

Em.name: Eratosthenian Mare
Em.desc: Low relative brightness plains with relatively few craters large enough to map,  patches of small domes, sharp-crested ridges, observable flow fronts.

EIp.name: Eratosthenian Imbrian Plateau
EIp.desc: Forms high standing plateaus (relative to the mare surfaces in Oceanus Procellarum) with domes, cones, and dark mantling materials.

Ic.name: Imbrian Crater, Undivided
Ic.desc: Subdued topographic relief compared to younger impact features, generally less than 40 km in diameter, with broad flat floors, and little to no ejecta present.

Ic1.name: Imbrian Crater, Lower
Ic1.desc: Similar description to unit Ic, craters mantled by materials of the Orientale group.

Ic2.name: Imbrian Crater, Upper
Ic2.desc: Similar description to unit Ic, craters superpose materials of the Orientale group.

Icc.name: Imbrian Crater, Catena
Icc.desc: Subdued and mantled elongated linear to elliptical clusters of circular to semi-circular depressions, often overlapping.

Isc.name: Imbrian Crater, Secondary
Isc.desc: Small diameter craters, densely spaced near and/or on the ejecta blanket of craters.

Icf.name: Imbrian Crater, Fracture Floor
Icf.desc: Crater floors typically domed, with furrows and/or  linear to curvilinear fractures with variable widths and depths. Blocks and material between the fractures sometimes reoriented.

Ib.name: Imbrian Basin, Undivided
Ib.desc: Gently rolling to hilly terrain containing aggregates of subdued irregular to circular craters. Also forms outer basin and ejecta of crater Schrodinger.

Ibm.name: Imbrian Basin, Massif
Ibm.desc: Rugged blocks forming arcuate raised ridges within crater Schrodinger.

Id.name: Imbrian Dark Mantle
Id.desc: Some of the lowest albedo material mapped, generally occurs near the outer margins of larger basins. Scalloped, smooth textures with small craters.

Ig.name: Imbrian Grooved
Ig.desc: Covers craters and other terrae of pre-Nectarian through Imbrian age. Craters have radial grooves on rims and walls with some mounds.

Iia.name: Imbrian Imbrium Alpes Formation
Iia.desc: Angular blocky and knobby with smooth, mantled surface. Closely spaced hills and hummocks, ~2-5 km in diameter.

Iiap.name: Imbrian Imbrium Apenninus Formation
Iiap.desc: Coarse blocks of material parallel to scarp bordering Imbrium basin. Smooth to undulating interblock materials.

Iic.name: Imbrian Imbrium Crater
Iic.desc: Individual craters <25 km diam., clusters and chains of craters <10 km diam. radial to Imbrium. Moderately subdued topographic features.

Iif.name: Imbrian Imbrium Fra Mauro Formation
Iif.desc: Sinuous, curvilinear, and straight ridges draping the surface below. Surface texture locally hummocky.

Im1.name: Imbrian Mare, Lower
Im1.desc: Forms flat, smooth surfaces. Relatively higher albedo compared to unit Im2 but lower albedo than unit Ip. High density of superposed craters.

Im2.name: Imbrian Mare, Upper
Im2.desc: Forms flat, smooth surfaces. Lower albedo and crater density than unit Im1. Numerous ridges. Difficult to distinguish from unit Id.

Imd.name: Imbrian Mare, Dome
Imd.desc: Steeply sloping, high-relief, rough domical or conical shaped edifices, sometimes with pitted summits.

Iohi.name: Imbrian Orientale Hevelius Formation, Inner Facies
Iohi.desc: Curvilinear to swirly ridges and troughs mostly radial and subradial to Orientale basin.

Ioho.name: Imbrian Orientale Hevelius Formation, Outer Facies
Ioho.desc: Swirly, lineated, hummocky and smooth materials forming a discontinuous and irregular boundary.

Ios.name: Imbrian Orientale Hevelius Formation, Secondary Crater Facies
Ios.desc: Overlapping crater chains and clusters radial and peripheral to the basin.

Iom.name: Imbrian Orientale Maunder Formation
Iom.desc: Smooth to rolling, intensely fractured plains with broad linear ridges and smooth domes.

Iork.name: Imbrian Orientale Montes Rook Formation, Knobby Facies
Iork.desc: Knobby, hummocky, rolling and chaotic materials with interstitial irregular grooves and depressions.

Iorm.name: Imbrian Orientale Montes Rook Formation, Massif Facies
Iorm.desc: High-relief, smooth blocks marking the second and third rings of the basin.

Ip.name: Imbrian Plains
Ip.desc: Smooth, flat to undulatory terrain of intermediate albedo occurring mostly in topographic lows and crater floors of Imbrian and older age.

It.name: Imbrian Terra
It.desc: Low relief, low crater density, moderate to high albedo, moderately smooth surface.

Itd.name: Imbrian Terra, Dome
Itd.desc: Outlines and characteristics similar to main-sequence craters, with smooth inner flanks, paucity of ejecta, inner terracing, secondary cratering.

INp.name: Imbrian Nectarian Plains
INp.desc: Smooth, flat to undulating surface, moderate to high density of superposed craters.

INt.name: Imbrian Nectarian Terra
INt.desc: Gently rolling terrain, moderate to high density of craters.

Nc.name: Nectarian Crater
Nc.desc: Considerably muted topographic relief compared to younger impact features, with broad flat floors typically another unit, and very little to no ejecta present.

Nb.name: Nectarian Basin, Undivided
Nb.desc: Material of raided walls and slumped blocks of basins, as well as aggregates of closely spaced subdued hills and ridges.

Nbl.name: Nectarian Basin, Lineated
Nbl.desc: Sharp, raised ridges, intervening flat areas or deep troughs and smooth hills with narrow grooves.

Nbm.name: Nectarian Basin, Massif
Nbm.desc: Rugged blocks most commonly 10 to 30 km across, forms highest and most rugged parts of arcuate raised ridges.

Nbsc.name: Nectarian Basin, Secondary Crater
Nbsc.desc: Grouped in clusters, chains and groove-like chains, mostly peripheral and approximately radial to Nectarian basins.

Nnj.name: Nectarian Nectaris Janssen Formation
Nnj.desc: Rolling subdued terrain having numerous linear features including ridges, scarps, and grooves radial to Nectaris basin.

Np.name: Nectarian Plains
Np.desc: Generally flat, moderate albedo terrain with dense population of large, old craters.

Nt.name: Nectarian Terra
Nt.desc: Moderately rough surface, rolling to moderately rugged overall relief, with diverse ages of superposed and buried craters.

Ntp.name: Nectarian Terra-Mantling and Plains
Ntp.desc: Light colored, wavy or rolling surfaces more heavily cratered than unit Ip.

pNb.name: pre-Nectarian Basin
pNb.desc: Subdued, eroded mountain rings and arcuate segments of rings, rim, walls, and inner-ring materials.

pNbm.name: pre-Nectarian Basin Massif
pNbm.desc: Large mountainous landforms commonly lying along arc, both continuous and discontinuous, gradational with generally finer-scale topography.

pNc.name: pre-Nectarian Crater
pNc.desc: Discontinuous, subdued rim crests and rounded, curved or straight rim remnants.

pNt.name: pre-Nectarian Terra
pNt.desc: Rugged, diverse terrain, degraded partial crater rims, gradational with smoother unit Nt, and rougher units pNbm and pNc.
